lots.guide_summary: No SOLD and no UNSOLD evidence. All surviving entries are dealer ASKING prices for single coins (per coin, not for the lot): about $40 to $60 for a circulated 1927 Canberra, $89 for an EF one, about $40 for a VF 1954 Royal Visit and about $39 for an EF 1952 (lead only). Common dates (1936, 1951, 1952, 1963) sell to dealers at about melt in circulated grades. Melt floor for the lot, at the dealer-site silver spot of AUD 87.71/oz (one source only, not cross-checked): 3 x .925 coins at 0.336 oz = about $88, plus 4 x .500 coins at 0.182 oz = about $64, so about $150 total. A rough lot value is $150 to $250 (melt plus a modest premium for the 1927 Canberra, 1954 Royal Visit and the 1910), but that is an estimate, not evidence. AUD throughout, no conversion.
lots.working: No SOLD entries survive, so both maximum bids are 0 under the rules. For context only (not a bid): melt about $150 / 1.198 = about $125 hammer is the price at which you pay only melt all-in. Buyer's premium 19.8%. Pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah, no freight.
lots.confidence_reason: Dates read from holder labels and partly confirmed on the coins (1927 Canberra, 1951 Jubilee, 1952, 1963, 1936 and the 1954 Royal Visit design are readable; the 1910 date on the coin is mostly lost in glare). Evidence is asking prices only, and the silver spot is a single unconfirmed source.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: (1) the researcher's $59.99 claim against the 1927 Fine-to-VF URL, because that page shows $39.99; refiled with the right price, and $59.99 moved to the separate VF pack URL. (2) 1927 Canberra aUnc $139 (page JSON opened, price confirmed) and Unc $299 (search JSON confirmed): much higher grade than this lot, not comparable. (3) 1951 Uncirculated $229 (search JSON confirmed): not comparable grade, and the title does not say Jubilee. (4) 1936 florin 'gEF' $12.95: the product page was never opened, the price looks wrong for an EF 1936, and I could not re-find it (429 and no 1936 match in the product search), so it is unverified and dropped. (5) 1933 VG $99 and the 1946-47 pair: different dates, context only. (6) 1910 PCGS AU53 $899 and 1963 PCGS MS65 $269: slabbed high grades, not comparable. (7) Silver spot AUD 87.71/oz: not a price for this item, so it was the wrong kind for an ASKING entry; moved into guide_summary as an unconfirmed melt guide.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. Holder labels read: 1910; F1065 1936; F 920 (yellow sticker); F1145 1927 Canb.; F1150 1951 Jub.; F1137 1963; F1019 1952 (with a crossed-out '934' sticker). Dealer pencil '2/-' on several. Enlarged, the F 920 coin shows a kangaroo standing behind a reclining lion, which is the 1954 Royal Visit florin, and the date is not legible. The 1910 is quite worn (about Fine) with glare across half the coin; the shield reverse and 'ONE FLORIN' legend can be seen. The 1927, 1951 and 1963 show some lustre. No obvious damage, but only the reverses are shown.
lots.condition: Circulated, roughly Fine (1910) to VF/EF (others). Only one side of each coin is visible; obverses, rims and any cleaning or edge knocks are not visible.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the F 920 coin is a 1954 Royal Visit florin, and that the 1910 really is dated 1910 (please show the obverse and the date)? Are any of the coins cleaned or damaged on the obverse or rims?
